name: tca_cycle
description: TCA / Citric Acid Cycle (Krebs Cycle). Central amphibolic pathway that oxidizes acetyl-CoA to CO₂ while generating reducing equivalents (NADH, FADH₂) and one GTP. Edges are formally linked to MetabolicMechanism objects.

nodes.label: Acetyl-CoA
nodes.notes: Two-carbon unit entering the cycle. Comes from pyruvate (PDH), β-oxidation, or ketogenic amino acids.

nodes.label: Oxaloacetate
nodes.notes: Four-carbon acceptor that is regenerated each turn. Also an important anaplerotic / gluconeogenic intermediate.

nodes.label: Citrate
nodes.notes: Six-carbon product of the first condensation. Can also signal high energy and inhibit glycolysis (PFK-1).

nodes.label: Isocitrate
nodes.notes: Isomer of citrate. Substrate for the first oxidative decarboxylation.

nodes.label: α-Ketoglutarate
nodes.notes: Five-carbon intermediate. Important precursor for glutamate and other amino acids (amphibolic).

nodes.label: Succinyl-CoA
nodes.notes: High-energy thioester. Precursor for porphyrins / heme. Also regulates its own production.

nodes.label: Succinate
nodes.notes: Four-carbon intermediate. Substrate of the only membrane-bound TCA enzyme (Complex II).

nodes.label: Malate
nodes.notes: Four-carbon intermediate. Can also be exported for gluconeogenesis (malate-aspartate shuttle).

edges.notes: Condenses the 2-carbon acetyl group with 4-carbon oxaloacetate. Highly exergonic / irreversible. Commits acetyl-CoA to the cycle.
Isomerization via cis-aconitate. Iron-sulfur cluster enzyme.
First oxidative decarboxylation. Produces NADH and releases the first CO₂.
Second oxidative decarboxylation. Produces NADH and the second CO₂. Irreversible.
Only substrate-level phosphorylation in the TCA cycle. Produces GTP (which can be converted to ATP). High-energy thioester is used.
Only membrane-bound TCA enzyme. Functions as Complex II of the electron transport chain. Produces FADH₂ instead of NADH.
Hydration reaction. Reversible and near equilibrium.
Regenerates oxaloacetate so the cycle can continue. Highly endergonic; pulled forward by continuous use of oxaloacetate by citrate synthase. Produces the third NADH.
